FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Hexaconazole + Zineb wettable powder is a fungicide for agricultural use. 


Hexaconazole + Zineb wettable powder is generally manufactured to contain Hexaconazole 4 percent m/m and 
Zineb 68 percent m/m. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 and 
the Rules framed there under. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16920 : 2018 


Indian Standard 


HEXACONAZOLE + ZINEB, WETTABLE 
POWDER (WP) — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, methods of 
sampling and test for the combination formulation of 
Hexaconazole + Zineb, Wettable Powder. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below:

3 REOUIREMENTS 
3.1 Constituents 


3.1.1 The material shall consist of hexaconazole 
technical and, zineb technical together with dispersing 
agent(s), wetting agent(s), suitable carrier(s) and other 
formulant(s). 


3.1.2 Hexaconazole technical and, zineb technical 
employed in the manufacture of the material shall 
conform to IS 14549 and IS 3898. 


3.2 Physical 


The material shall comply with 
requirements specified in 3.2.1 to 3.2.4. 


the physical 


3.2.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of yellow powder free 
from hard lumps and shall wet readily on mixing with 
water providing a suspension suitable for use as spray. 


3.2.2 Sieving Requirement 


When determined by the method specified in 11.1 of 
IS 6940, the amount of material passing through 75 
micron IS sieve [see IS 460 (Part 1)], shall not be less 
than 98 percent by mass. 


3.2.3 Suspensibility 


The suspensibility shall not be less than 75 percent by 
mass, when tested by the method specified in 11.2 of 
IS 6940. 


3.2.4 Wettability 


The time when the whole material gets completely 
submerged in water shall not exceed 120 s when tested 
by the method specified in 11.4 of IS 6940. 


3.3 Chemical 


The material shall comply with chemical requirements 
specified in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


3.3.1 Hexaconazole and Zineb Content 


When determined by the method prescribed in Annex 
A for hexaconazole content and Annex B for zineb 
content, the observed hexaconazole percent (w/w) and 
zineb content percent (w/w) of any of the samples, 
shall not be differ from the declared nominal value 
by more than the percent tolerance limits indicated 
below: 


Nominal Value, Tolerance limits, 


Percent Percent of the 
Nominal Value 
Up to 9 + 10 
-5 
Above 9 and below 50 + 
50 and above +5 
-3 


IS 16920 : 2018 


3.3.2 Acidity or Alkalinity 


When tested by the method specified in 11.3 of IS 6940, 
the acidity (as H,SO,) or alkalinity (as NaOH) of the 
material shall be 0.5 percent by mass, max. 


4 SAMPLING 


When freshly manufactured material in bulk quantity 
and/or the retail pack of the formulated product is/ 
are offered for inspection, representative sample of 
the material shall be drawn and tested as prescribed in 
IS 10627, and if tested within 90 days of its date of 
manufacture, the criteria for conformity shall be that 
the contents, in percent (m/m), shall not be less than the 
declared nominal value. The upper limit for conformity 
shall be the same as those given in 3.3.1. 


When the material is offered for inspection after 
90 days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done 
as prescribed in IS 10627. However, the criteria for 
conformity of the material, when tested, shall be the 
limits of tolerances, as applicable on the declared 
nominal value as given under 3.3.1. 


5 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in trilaminated pouches 
comprising of PET/aluminium foil/LDPE. The 
pouches shall be heat sealed to make it leak proof 
and pilfer proof. The trilaminated pouches up to | kg 
capacity shall be inserted in duplex board up to 250 g 
mass and 3 ply CFB E — flute carton for 500 g and 
1 Kg as secondary pack. All types of containers shall 
further be packed in corrugated fiberboard boxes as per 
IS 2771 (Part 1). The container shall also comply with 
the general requirements specified in IS 8190 (Part 1). 


6 MARKING 


6.1 The containers shall be securely closed and, shall 
bear legibly and indelibly the following information 
in addition to any other information as required under 


the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed there 
under: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal hexaconazole and zineb content, percent 
(m/m), 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the /nsecticides 
Act, 1968, and Rules framed thereunder; and 


j) Any other information required under the Legal 
Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. 


6.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


6.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of the conditions under which the licence for use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate methods 
referred to in 3.2.2 to 3.2.4 and 3.3.1 to 3.3.2. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 16920 : 2018 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 3.3.1 ) 


DETERMINATION OF HEXACONAZOLE CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


A-1.1 Hexaconazole content is determined by Gas 
Liquid Chromatography (GLC), method using internal 
standard technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 Gas Liquid Chromatograph 
A Gas Liquid chromatograph equipped with flame 


ionization detector coupled to chromatography 

software and, printer is used. 

Instrument GLC with FID coupled 

Column Glass length 2.0 m, ID 3 mm, 
packed with 5 percent OV-101 
on Chromosorb WHP, 80/100 
mesh 

Flow rate Nitrogen 30 ml/min, Hydrogen 


30 ml/min, air 300 ml/min 
20ul 
Oven temperature : 250°C 


Injection volume 
Temperatures 
Injector temperature : 280°C 
Detector temperature : 280°C 
A-2.2 Analytical Balance 
A-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 10 ul capacity 
A-2.4 Ultrasonic Bath 
A-2.5 Standard Glassware 


A-3 REAGENTS 


A-3.1 Chloroform — AR grade, or equivalent 


A-3.2 Internal Standard, Dioctyl Phthalate — AR 
grade, or equivalent 


A-3.3 Standard Hexaconazole — of known purity. 
A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution: 


Weigh accurately about 1.0 g of dioctyl phthalate into 
a 100 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in chloroform and 
make up the volume up to the mark with chloroform. 
Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately about 0.1 g of hexaconazole reference 
standard of known purity into a 25 ml volumetric flask. 


Add 5 ml of the internal standard solution (A-4.1), 
sonicate and make up to the mark with chloroform. 
Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh 2.5 g hexaconazole + zineb WP formulation 
sample into 25 ml volumetric flask. Add 10 ml 
chloroform, shake well and filter. Add 5 ml chloroform 
again, shake well and filter. Add 5 ml chloroform and 
pool all filtrate in another 25 ml volumetric flask. Now 
add 5 ml internal standard (see A-4.1), sonicate and 
make up the volume with chloroform. Shake well to 
homogenize and inject. 


A-4.4 Estimation 


A-4.4.1 Inject 1 ul standard solution until the internal 
standard / reference substance area quotients of two 
successive chromatograms do not deviate from each 
other by more than 2 percent. Then use the following 
injection sequence: 


REN BEI AA 


Ç = 
S = 


Standard Solution, and 


Sample solution (1, 2, ....... ,n) 


From the chromatograms of the standard solution and 
sample solution, measure the peak areas of the internal 
standard and Hexaconazole peaks, and compute the 
percentage of the Hexaconazole as given in A-6. 


A- 5 RETENTION TIME (GUIDE VALUES) 


A-5.1 Hexaconazole — 3.8 min. 


A-5.2 Dioctyl phthalate (Internal standard) — 
9.3 min. 


A-5.3 Total Run Time — 12 min.

with internal standard is given in Fig. 1.

ANNEX B 
( Clause 3.3.1 ) 


DETERMINATION OF ZINEB CONTENT 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


Zineb is digested with sulphuric acid and, liberated 
carbon disulphide is absorbed in alcoholic potassium 
hydroxide. Potassium methyl xanthate so produced is 
titrated with iodine. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 Zineb Determination Assembly 


The apparatus shall be as described in IS 3898 and 
consists of a 200 ml flask fitted with condenser with 
outlet tube connected to two absorbers and a 500 ml 
filter flask serving as a bubbler. The latter in turn is 
connected to a source of mild suction. 


B-2.2 Glass Vial — 15 mm x 25 mm 


B-2.3 Glasswares 
B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 Lead Acetate Solution — 10 percent (m/v) 
B-3.2 Sulphuric Acid — 1.1 N 


B-3.3 Solution of Potassium Hydroxide in 
Methanol — 2 N 


B-3.4 Dilute Acetic Acid — 30 percent (v/v) 
B-3.5 Standard Iodine Solution — 0.1 N 
B-3.6 Starch Indicator Solution — Freshly prepared 


B-3.7 Phenolphthalein Indicator Solution — 1 
percent (m/v) in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


B-4.1 Determination of Blank 


Pipette 25 ml of the 2 N methanolic potassium 
hydroxide solution in a 500 ml wide mouth Erlenmeyer 
flask containing 250 ml distilled water. Add 3 drops 
of phenolphthalein indicator solution and titrate with 
30 percent acetic acid solution till just neutral. Add 
5 ml starch indicator solution and titrate against 0.1 N 
iodine solution. If more than 0.1 ml of iodine solution 
is consumed, the methanolic potassium hydroxide 
solution cannot be used for the determination of zineb 
content. 


B-4.2 Determination of Active Ingredient 


Transfer 25 ml of 10 percent lead acetate solution by 
pipette to the lead acetate trap (Absorber No. 1) and 
25 ml of 2 N potassium hydroxide to the potash trap 
(Absorber No. 2). 


Transfer a quantity of sample equivalent to 0.2 to 0.3 g 
of zineb to an accurately weighed clean dry glass vial. 
Wipe outside of the vial with a tissue and, reweigh the 
vial plus the sample accurately to determine the exact 
mass of the sample. Place the vial in the 200 ml flask 
and connect it back to the assembly. Close the needle 
valve and connect the assembly to the vacuum line. 
Slowly, open the valve and adjust the rate of bubbling 
in the absorbers to 2 to 6 bubbles per second. Turn 
on the cooling water and maintain the temperature 
of the water jacket at 10 °C (4 2 °C) throughout the 
experiment. By graduated cylinder add carefully 
50 ml of boiling 1.1 N sulphuric acid through the inlet 
tube of the distillation head. Make sure, that the inlet 
tube dips in the liquid. Turn on the heating mantle and 
heat carefully so as not to allow the solution to spurt 
into the condenser. Continue the heating and bubbling 
for exactly 1 h and 45 min. After the digestion is 
completed, quickly disconnect the potash trap and, 
rinse the contents into a 500 ml Erlenmeyer flask, 
containing about 250 ml distilled water. Add 3 drops 
of phenolphthalein indicator solution and titrate the 
solution immediately with 30 percent acetic acid until 
the solution is just neutral. Cool and then titrate the 
neutralized solution immediately with 0.1 N iodine 
solution using starch indicator till the colour changes 
to violet. 


B-5 CALCULATION 


. (Y, -V,)x N x 13.79 
Zineb content, percent by mass = ——— 


M 
where, 

V, = volume of iodine solution required for the 
sample, in ml; 

V, = volume of iodine solution required for the 
blank, in ml; 

N = normality of the iodine solution used; and 

M = mass of the sample taken for the test, in g.
